method: Readability.js (2,812 lines) and Readability-readerable.js read in full for behaviour, JSDOMParser.js read for structure (its node, element, attribute, style and tokenizer classes; no network or file access, no behaviour beyond building a tree), index.js and index.d.ts for the option surface; behaviour described in ECDEV's words, no code copied. The pinned commit was cloned into an isolated scratch directory and not kept.
licence_note: The repository is Apache-2.0, but JSDOMParser.js (37 KB) is MPL-2.0 by its own header: file-level licences are mixed. Nothing here copies either; legal conclusions are not made.

rows.behaviour: Takes visible p, pre, article (and parents of div > br) outside unlikely-candidate class/id patterns and not in li p; each with at least 140 characters adds sqrt(length - 140); true once the sum passes 20
rows.note: ECDEV reports the numbers (main characters, long lines, the square-root score), not a verdict. Live, 10 pages (2026-10-07): JavaScript app shells 0 characters (Open Prices, Mastodon explore, Bluesky); Wikipedia Matcha 50,912 characters and score 1,487; Allbirds story 117; Rothy's about 41; BBC news 20; Decathlon contact 12; GitHub changelog 8; Hacker News 3,881 characters and score 0 (a list, no long lines). The donor's article threshold of 20 does not fit store pages, which is why no verdict is drawn.

rows.behaviour: Scores candidate containers: tag base scores (div +5; pre, td, blockquote +3; lists and form -3; headings -5), class/id weight of 25 either way, text length per 100 characters (capped at 3) and comma count, spread to ancestors at full, half and a third of the score, discounted by link density where fragment links count 0.3
rows.note: ECDEV selects main content by the main landmark and falls back to the whole page without chrome landmarks. Live, 6 of 10 pages declared a main landmark; Hacker News (table layout) and three app shells did not. A scored fallback can only matter for pages like the first.

rows.behaviour: Class and id vocabulary (comment, footer, sidebar, social, sponsor, related, shoutbox, pager...) marks a container unlikely unless it also matches article, body, column, content, main
rows.note: A chrome signal beyond landmarks and ARIA roles; on product pages words like related and social can wrap real content, so it needs measuring against product page captures before use.

rows.behaviour: Strips a site-name tail after the last ' | - – — \ / > » ' separator when the rest keeps at least 3 words, falls back to a colon split or a single h1 when the title is very long or short, and reverts to the original title when the result has 4 words or fewer
rows.note: ECDEV takes product titles from structured data and keeps the page title as stated; whether separator cleanup recovers a product name better than the stated title is unmeasured.

rows.behaviour: Takes the first application/ld+json block (CDATA wrapper removed) that is an article type, found directly, in an array, or under @graph; requires a schema.org @context (string or object with @vocab); resolves name versus headline by text similarity above 0.75 with the page title
rows.note: ECDEV reads every JSON-LD block, arrays and @graph, ProductGroup variants and Product offers, and takes no article metadata. It does not check @context, so a Product type in a non-schema.org vocabulary would be read as schema.org: see readability.jsonld-context-check.

rows.behaviour: Ignores a JSON-LD block whose @context is not schema.org, including an object context whose @vocab is not
rows.note: How often a non-schema.org context names a Product on live store pages is unmeasured; the donor's rule is cheap and refuses rather than guesses.

rows.behaviour: Byline, excerpt, site name and published time from JSON-LD, then dc:, og:, twitter: and plain meta tags in a fixed precedence, entities unescaped
rows.note: Article metadata is not product evidence; ECDEV keeps page metadata and structured product data as stated.

rows.behaviour: A node is invisible when its inline display is none, its visibility is hidden, it has the hidden attribute, or aria-hidden is true (unless it is a fallback image)
rows.note: Gap found and closed: ECDEV's text capture skipped script, style and similar tags but counted text hidden by its own markup. It now skips the hidden attribute and inline display:none and visibility:hidden; it deliberately leaves aria-hidden (hidden from assistive technology, not from sight) and evaluates no stylesheets. Live, 2 of 10 saved pages lost one visible line each (353 to 352, 1,056 to 1,055).

rows.behaviour: Recovers real image sources from noscript fallbacks and lazy-load attributes (data-src and similar) so reader output shows pictures
rows.note: ECDEV keeps no pictures (tests pin that image URLs are not stored); the lazy-loading attribute vocabulary is the only reusable fact.

rows.behaviour: Rewrites the chosen content for display: drops empty or link-heavy blocks and forms, strips styles and classes, makes links absolute, merges nested wrappers, turns br runs into paragraphs
rows.note: Reader-view transforms. ECDEV hashes and compares visible text and keeps source bytes unchanged as evidence; a rewritten DOM would be a derived document, not a capture.

rows.behaviour: A minimal DOM parser for worker use that needs well-formed markup (no live NodeLists), and the option surface: charThreshold 500, nbTopCandidates 5, maxElemsToParse, keepClasses, classesToPreserve, disableJSONLD, linkDensityModifier, serializer
rows.note: ECDEV parses with an HTML5 parser (html5ever through scraper); a forgiving-markup parser is the opposite of what the donor's own header warns about.

file_coverage.rule: every FIRST_PARTY_SOURCE path in the census files.jsonl matches the first prefix below; checked by tools/commerce/validate.py --records-only

entries.capabilities: readability.content-scoring, unlikely-candidate-patterns, title-cleanup, jsonld-selection, jsonld-context-check, article-metadata, visibility, image-unwrapping, reader-output-rewriting

tooling only: lint configuration, no behaviour
